newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-IPE Brent uncertainty may wake up the bear.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-IPE Brent uncertainty may wake up the bear.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - July 21

* The market remains in a "broadening formation" which indicates uncertainty and may yield to a bearish influence eventually. * The September Brent chart remains in upside corrective mode from the June 20 low around $17.70 but its rise is being barred by stiff downtrend resistance which stems from the $20.40 high on May 16.

IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures are seen in a broadening upwardly corrective phase in the short term, but some analysts warn that uncertainty leading to volatility could easily turn the mood bearish.
The September Brent chart remains in upside corrective mode from the June 20 low around $17.70 but its rise is being barred by stiff downtrend resistance which stems from the May 16 high of $20.40.

The contract bounced off this line on Friday at $18.70 after an unconvincing break to $18.80 on Thursday, but is underpinned to the downside by the recent period of congestion and psychological support around $18 a barrel.
"All action since $17.68 on June 20 is still firmly viewed as corrective in nature," Al Graham at Elliott Wave International said.
"This pattern could unfold in several different ways, no variation stands out above the rest and it is unclear whether it is complete above $18.99," he added.

Independent analyst Elli Gifford said the market remains in a "broadening formation" which indicates uncertainty and may yield to a bearish influence eventually, though cautiously she said momentum indicators were still in oversold condition, flagging buy signals.
"There is a lot of uncertainty and volatility in the market that makes me think the next major move may be down," Gifford said.
Peter Sceats analyst at CharTech-MCS took a more neutral to bullish stance short term expecting the uptrend to hold for now.
"The market showed signs of life on the upside last week as the uptrend on the spot month continuation and weekly charts stayed intact and a mini double bottom was posted," Sceats said.

However he added: "Background technicals remain negative, you've go to go with the up moves when they come but realise that while the current overall technical profile prevails they are likely to be short lived" he added.
Sceats defines the reconfiguration of a six-week uptrend on the spot month continuation chart that takes into account the mini double bottom at $17.80 from Monday and Tuesday of last week.
"Join the $17.32 (June 11) and $17.49 (June 20) lows with $17.80 (double bottom) and you will see what we believe the most important short term technical pattern on the chart".
Gas oil too was seen moving broadly sideways but with the rally of the past two weeks running out of steam and sentiment turning bearish, though $160 remains sturdy support.
"The rally of the past two weeks looks in serious trouble so it could well gain a downward trend rather than hold its upward bias," Elli Gifford said.
September Brent on SIMEX was quoted at $18.05/$18.14 a barrel.
August NYMEX crude, trading on the out-of-hours ACCESS system, was last done at $19.23, down four cents from New York's close.

WTI suffered marked technical damage. August crude settled below its nine and 14-day simple moving average. Analysts said August crude now hovered just 25 cents or so away from breaking a trendline extending from June 20 on the spot continuation chart.
If the trendline support is broken analysts expect a test of the $18.35 a 16-month low for spot crude and seen by some as a good bottoming point.
